facts.value: Frederick MacMonnies's Bacchante, placed by Charles McKim in the library's courtyard fountain, was attacked by a small powerful group as vice-ridden and treason to virtue. Most Bostonians supported it, according to the Cleveland Museum of Art.
facts.quote: treason to purity and sobriety and virtue
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://www.clevelandart.org/print/art/1919.589' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'treason to purity and sobriety and virtue'
